messages:
From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@nextmesa.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 jump + 502s on private VPC since 08:50 — logs attached

Ben —

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95/p99 latency and an increase in 502s on our private deployment (region us-west-2) starting around 08:50 PDT. Throughput dropped ~40% compared to yesterday's baseline and our nightly batch jobs are timing out.

We attached a small bundle of logs and traces (nextmesa_logs_0627.tar.gz) — there are repeated decoder timeouts and a cluster-level 502 spike tied to encoder nodes. No config changes on our side; this looks like something on your side related to the encoder path.

Can you triage ASAP? Our SRE team is on standby (sre@nextmesa.com). Given this is customer-facing traffic we need ETA on mitigation and whether a temporary canary rollback to the previous model/quantization profile is possible.

Thanks,
Maya Chen
Director of AI Ops
NextMesa Inc.

(attachment: nextmesa_logs_0627.tar.gz)

Maya —

Thanks for the alert and the logs. I’m escalating to our SRE + private deployment on-call now (cc'd). Initial read: the pattern you described (encoder timeouts + 502s + throughput drop) aligns with a regression we saw in an opportunistic kernel selection roll last night in us-west-2 that affected certain model/sequence length pairs.

Immediate plan:
- Vivek and I will triage the traces and produce an exec-friendly summary in the next 90 minutes.
- If the regression maps to the new kernel path, we will trigger a targeted canary rollback to the previous variant for your tenant to restore baseline.
- If rollback is not fast enough, we will propose an on-the-wire mitigation (adjust batching and reduce KV cache TTL to avoid cold misses).

Can you confirm whether you can accept a short canary rollback window (5–10 minutes) and whether there are any in-flight releases on your side? Also flag any regulatory windows we should avoid.

Ben Carter

Subject: Internal: NextMesa VPC — triage + immediate mitigations

Vivek / Laura —

Pulling you in for an urgent triage. Key facts from Maya's logs: encoder decode latency spikes coincident with a kernel-selection change pushed in autoscaler last night. Repro at p99 for token lengths between 512–1024. Impact: ~40% throughput drop, elevated 502s from encoder pool.

Please start with:
1) map error traces to kernel id and config (I suspect adaptive kernel that landed 02:14 UTC).
2) confirm whether the canary rollback for NextMesa tenant is safe and what cluster impact looks like (blast radius).
3) short-term mitigations we can flip server side (batch sizing, soft-quantization fallback, reduce KV cache TTL).

If rollback is viable, coordinate with Maya for a 10-min window immediately (they gave go-ahead). I will prepare an exec summary for Ops/CTO and the NextMesa leadership.

Ben

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: NextMesa VPC — triage + immediate mitigations

Ben / Laura —

Initial findings (60m triage):
- The traces reference kernel_ilm_v2 which our deployment pipeline replaced for certain encoder tensors last night. kernel_ilm_v2 shows regression for medium-length sequences on our GPU family (A4500 equivalent).
- Root cause candidate: a fallback path that increases attention scratch memory and causes stalls when sequence length distribution crosses 512 tokens. This leads to request timeouts and 502s when the encoder pool saturates.

Recommended immediate actions (safe, reversible):
A) Canary rollback for NextMesa tenant to kernel_ilm_v1 for encoder workers (10-minute window) — low risk for other tenants if targeted by tenant routing.
B) If we need additional breathing room: reduce max_batch_size by 20% and enable double-prefetch guard to smooth encoder load. This will reduce throughput but should cut p99 and 502s.
C) Short post-mitigation tune: increase KV cache hit threshold and tighten batching window from 64ms -> 40ms to avoid spike alignment.

I will prepare a short runbook and push traces to the drive folder. If Ben wants, I can run the canary rollback within 15 minutes and monitor metrics with Maya.

Vivek Kulkarni
SRE Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood_trace_request_0627.json)

Subject: NextMesa incident readout + proposed actions (canary rollback scheduled)

Maya —

Thank you for the quick turnaround and permission for a canary window. Summary and next steps:

Summary:
- Impact: p99 latency increased, throughput -40%, elevated 502s on encoder pool for sequences ~512–1024 tokens.
- Probable cause: kernel_ilm_v2 kernel selection introduced last night produced stalls under medium-length sequences on your node class.

Immediate mitigation (scheduled):
- We will perform a tenant-scoped canary rollback to kernel_ilm_v1 on your encoder workers at 13:10 PDT for a 10-minute window. Vivek will monitor key signals (p50/p95/p99, 502 rate, throughput) and will revert immediately if any adverse side effects occur.

Follow-up actions (post-mitigation):
- Complete a targeted kernel performance audit for A4500-class GPUs and block kernel_ilm_v2 until fixes are validated. (Jira OPS-9842)
- Adjust batching defaults and KV cache thresholds for your tenant; schedule a controlled rollout next week during off-peak.
- Provide an exec-friendly postmortem within 24 hours, and a technical writeup within 72 hours.

Attachments and links: drive folder with traces and a canary snapshot (canary_snapshot_0627.tgz).

Does NextMesa want Redwood to proceed with the 13:10 canary now? Please reply "GO" to confirm and we will execute. Note: we will avoid NextMesa's compliance window (11:00–11:30 PDT) per your note.

Ben Carter
